title.es: Redactar el resumen de un segmento

es: Escribir un resumen fiel de un segmento de audio con tres verbos de habla, según + hablante y la postura de cada participante.

teaching.en: The summary should be faithful: it keeps the main points and does not add new opinions.
teaching.es: El resumen debe ser fiel: mantiene los puntos principales y no añade opiniones nuevas.
teaching.explanationEs: Fiel = cuenta lo que se dijo, no lo que tú piensas.
segments: The summary should be faithful: it keeps the
main points and does not add new opinions.
teaching.audioText: The summary should be faithful: it keeps the main points and does not add new opinions.

teaching.en: According to the guest, phones are useful tools, whereas the host is more cautious.
teaching.es: Según el invitado, los móviles son herramientas útiles, mientras que el presentador es más cauteloso.
teaching.explanationEs: According to + persona atribuye la idea; whereas contrasta dos posturas.
segments: According to the guest, phones are useful
tools, whereas the host is more cautious.
teaching.audioText: According to the guest, phones are useful tools, whereas the host is more cautious.

teaching.en: The guest sounds confident because she claims that a ban does not teach self-control.
teaching.es: La invitada suena segura porque afirma que una prohibición no enseña autocontrol.
teaching.explanationEs: La postura se describe con sounds + adjetivo y se apoya en un verbo de habla.
segments: The guest sounds confident because she claims
that a ban does not teach self-control.

teaching.en: The host raises a concern: too much screen time affects sleep.
teaching.es: El presentador plantea una preocupación: demasiado tiempo de pantalla afecta al sueño.
teaching.explanationEs: Raise a concern = plantear una preocupación.

teaching.en: A good summary can highlight the stance of each speaker with verbs like claim, admit or warn.
teaching.es: Un buen resumen puede destacar la postura de cada hablante con verbos como claim, admit o warn.
teaching.explanationEs: El verbo de habla ya muestra la actitud: claim afirma, admit concede, warn advierte.

teaching.en: Overall, the segment shows that both speakers want the same result: better learning.
teaching.es: En conjunto, el segmento muestra que ambos hablantes quieren el mismo resultado: aprender mejor.
teaching.explanationEs: Overall cierra el resumen con una valoración general.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es un resumen fiel de lo que dicen los dos hablantes?

choices.text: The guest loves phones and the host hates them.
The guest and the host agree that there should be a ban.
The guest thinks a ban is too strict, but the host is not sure.

feedback.es: Recoge lo que dice cada uno sin exagerar: la invitada ve la prohibición demasiado estricta y el presentador duda.

hint.es: Un resumen fiel no exagera ni añade opiniones.

origin.text:
GUEST: «I think a ban is too strict.»
HOST: «I am not sure.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Según la invitada, los móviles son útiles.»

feedback.es: According to atribuye la idea a una persona sin repetir she thinks.

hint.es: Sirve para atribuir una idea a otra persona.

origin.text: ___ to the guest, phones are useful.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El presentador suena más cauteloso que la invitada.»

answer.text: The host sounds more cautious than the guest

feedback.es: Sounds + adjetivo comparativo (more cautious) + than introduce la comparación.

hint.es: Sounds va seguido de un adjetivo, no de un adverbio.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de resumen con el matiz de su verbo.

pairs: The coach claims that the team is ready.
The captain admits that the team plays badly.
The doctor warns that the floor is wet.

feedback.es: Claim afirma, admit concede algo incómodo y warn advierte de un peligro.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la postura del estudiante.

choices.text: He is confident that phones help.
He agrees completely with the teacher.

feedback.es: El estudiante, sin embargo, teme que sean una distracción: su postura es la preocupación.

origin.audio: According to the teacher, phones are useful tools. The student, however, worries that they are a distraction. In the end, the two speakers want the same thing: better marks.

prompt.es: ¿Qué resumen es fiel a lo que dice la invitada?

choices.text: The guest denies that the plan is expensive.
The guest refuses to talk about the price.
The guest admits that the plan is expensive but claims that it saves money.

feedback.es: Reconoce el coste (admit) y afirma que ahorra dinero (claim): el resumen mantiene las dos ideas.

origin.text:
HOST: «Is the plan too expensive?»
GUEST: «It costs a lot, I admit, but it saves money in the long run.»

prompt.es: Completa tres frases de un resumen.

feedback.es: Whereas contrasta las dos posturas, concern nombra la preocupación y overall cierra con una valoración general.

sentences: The guest sounds confident, ___ the host is more cautious.
The host raises a ___ about sleep.
___, the segment shows two different stances.
origin.text: Traducción: «La invitada suena segura, mientras que el presentador es más cauteloso.» «El presentador plantea una preocupación sobre el sueño.» «En conjunto, el segmento muestra dos posturas distintas.»

prompt.es: Resume el segmento en 105-230 palabras: tres verbos de habla y la postura de cada uno.

answer.text: In this Tech Talk segment, the host and a teacher, Sara, discuss whether schools should ban phones. Sara claims that a phone is a strong learning tool, because students can search for information and take notes. She admits that some students play games in class, but she suggests using phones only for clear tasks. She also points out that too much screen time affects sleep, so she warns students not to use their phones late at night. The host is more cautious: he says he is still not sure and thinks that a full ban is easier to control. Sara disagrees, because in her opinion a ban does not teach self-control, and she recommends a three-month test in one school. Overall, the host sounds doubtful, whereas the guest sounds confident and practical.
accepted: In this Tech Talk segment, the host and a teacher, Sara, discuss whether schools should ban phones. Sara claims that a phone is a strong learning tool, because students can search for information and take notes. She admits that some students play games in class, but she suggests using phones only for clear tasks. She also points out that too much screen time affects sleep, so she warns students not to use their phones late at night. The host is more cautious: he says he is still not sure and thinks that a full ban is easier to control. Sara disagrees, because in her opinion a ban does not teach self-control, and she recommends a three-month test in one school. Overall, the host sounds doubtful, whereas the guest sounds confident and practical.

The segment is a talk between a host and Sara about phones in class. According to the guest, phones are useful because students can use a dictionary and take notes. She admits that they can be a distraction and suggests using them only for clear tasks. She also warns that late screen time affects sleep. The host raises a concern: parents worry that children become tired and anxious, and he thinks a full ban is easier to control. The guest answers that a ban does not teach self-control and recommends a short test in one school. Overall, the guest sounds confident, whereas the host is more cautious. It is a clear and balanced discussion.

feedback.es: Un buen resumen presenta el tema, atribuye las ideas con verbos de habla variados, indica la postura de cada uno y cierra con overall.

origin.text:
HOST: Welcome back to Tech Talk. Today our topic is phones in the classroom. Our guest is Sara, a teacher and researcher. Sara, should schools ban phones?
GUEST: I do not think so. A phone is a strong tool: students can search for information, use a dictionary and take notes.
HOST: But many students use their phones to play games or chat with friends.
GUEST: That is true, and I admit that it is a problem. Even so, I suggest using phones only for clear tasks and putting them away when the task is finished.
HOST: Some parents worry that children will become tired and anxious.
GUEST: I understand. The research points out that too much screen time affects sleep, so I warn students not to use their phones late at night.
HOST: I am still not sure. I think a full ban is easier to control.
GUEST: A ban is easy, but it does not teach self-control. I recommend trying a three-month test in one school.
HOST: Interesting. Before we go, thank you, Sara. That is all for today.

prompt.es: ¿Qué resumen muestra que el invitado concede un punto?

choices.text: The guest admits that some students play games.
The guest claims that no student plays games.
The guest denies that there is a problem.

feedback.es: Dice que es cierto y que es un problema: concede un punto, que se resume con admit.

origin.text: GUEST: «Yes, some students use phones to play games. That is a problem.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «El resumen debe ser fiel al hablante.»

answer.text: The summary must be faithful to the speaker

feedback.es: Un resumen fiel conserva las ideas del hablante sin añadir opiniones propias.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada adjetivo o verbo de postura con su significado.

feedback.es: Son las palabras para describir la postura de un hablante y la calidad de un resumen.
